subject: Realtime API: intermittent silent chunks and 503 surge
messages:
From: Anika Patel <anika@brightframe.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightframe Platform <ops@brightframe.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Realtime API - intermittent silent chunks and 503 surge

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing recurring gaps in the streaming transcript for our live captions feature starting ~07:58 UTC today. The client receives partial token streams then a ~3-12s silence window before the next chunk arrives; during the same windows we're observing a spike in 503 responses from the /v1/realtime endpoint. This has been intermittent but reproducible during load tests and a few production sessions (attached log).

Impact: viewer-facing captions freeze for short bursts (~5-10s) and retry logic on our side produces latency spikes. Error rate for our sessions jumped from ~0.8% to 6.7% during the window. Throughput appears reduced — concurrent streams show elevated backpressure and a small number of host disconnects.

We captured a short websocket trace and a server-side token timeline (attached). Can you triage? This is customer-impacting for our November live events.

Thanks,
Anika
Anika Patel

Thanks Anika — I pulled the trace and attached a tcpdump snippet. Quick notes from initial triage:

- We see repeated HTTP/1.1 chunked frames with incomplete final-chunk markers for a subset of connections, followed by an upstream 502/504 cascade at the proxy layer that manifests as 503 to the client.
- Keepalive resets appear correlated with peak CPU on the edge proxy (approx 78-92% for a narrow time window), coincident with a burst of small streaming requests from Brightframe (high concurrency + short TTLs).
- There's evidence of our dynamic batching threshold compaction kicking in: when the local batcher reduces batch size aggressively (to keep latency SLO), some partially framed responses appear to be delayed until buffer flush conditions are met — producing the silent chunk windows you see.

Hypothesis: a conjunction of (1) increased short-lived concurrency from Brightframe's load pattern, (2) batcher compaction logic hitting an edge case with chunk framing, and (3) transient proxy CPU pressure.

Immediate mitigations I can perform now:
- Force disable batcher compaction for Brightframe's routing policy (will drop some throughput efficiency but should eliminate coalescing-induced silences).
- Move their traffic to a less-loaded proxy pool / dedicate an extra worker set for the next 6 hours.

I've created JIRA-4821 and uploaded the tcpdump (attached). I'll instrument additional counters and post a follow-up in 30m with telemetry.

—Dev
Dev Patel

Quick telemetry snapshot: attaching an error-rate screenshot and a short metrics excerpt. Observations:

- Error rate (5m window) for Brightframe routing jumped to 6.2% at 07:58 UTC; token latency p50->p95 widened from 110ms->1.1s during the peaks.
- There was a small infra deployment 07:45 UTC affecting proxy image rotation in one US region; the deployment completed, but edge CPU spiked afterwards. We're correlating logs now.

Recommended immediate actions (operational):
1) Accept Dev's mitigation: disable compaction for Brightframe and shift traffic to a warm pool.
2) Open a canary rollback of the proxy image to last-stable for the affected nodes if CPU doesn't stabilize within 30 minutes.
3) Schedule an executive update if we expect >1 hour of customer impact or SLA risk.

Subject: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — Brightframe realtime degradation (customer-impacting)

Team — flagged for exec attention, Brightframe is experiencing intermittent streaming silences and a transient 503 spike that materially degrades their live captions. Impact window started 2027-11-10 07:58 UTC and is ongoing in short bursts.

Customer impact: viewer-facing caption freezes, elevated retry latency, potential hit to revenue for scheduled live events this week. Brightframe has requested an incident lead and ETA to full resolution.

Technical summary: Dev has identified chunk-framing delays caused by batcher compaction interacting poorly with proxy pressure after a recent edge image rotation. Mitigation applied: compaction disabled for Brightframe routing and traffic moved to a warm proxy pool. Early telemetry shows reduction in silent windows but not full elimination.

Business ask: Brightframe is a mid-enterprise account with upcoming live shows. They have requested a goodwill credit to cover impact; they're asking for a substantial concession. I recommend we pre-approve up to $20,000 in credits to be negotiated by Sales/CS if the incident exceeds 2 hours of visible customer disruption. Please confirm approval or counterproposal.

Planned next steps:
- Short exec call with Brightframe (propose 16:00 UTC today).
- Ops to complete proxy rollback if CPU doesn't normalize within 45m.
- Postmortem + runbook updates to be shared within 48h.

I need an OK on the credit ceiling and permission for a temporary dedicated routing for the customer for the next 24h (to be charged to incident budget).

—Rachel
